clues.text: This is the capital of a small island land in Europe. It sits between two deep harbours, and it is the farthest south capital in all of Europe.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside southern Europe and its island capitals

source.quote: Located between the Grand Harbour to the east and Marsamxett Harbour to the west

clues.text: This city was named the sunniest city in Europe in 2016. Its bright days set it apart from grey capitals far to the north.
clues.narrowing: rules out grey, wet capitals and narrows to sunny southern Europe

source.quote: Valletta was also listed as the sunniest city in Europe in 2016.

clues.text: Its stone buildings went up in the 1500s, built by knights. Those knights had held the island through a great siege by Ottoman foes.
clues.narrowing: rules out capitals not built by knights after an Ottoman siege

source.quote: Valletta's 16th-century buildings were constructed by the Knights Hospitaller.

clues.text: It packs 320 old monuments into a space smaller than many parks. People call it an open-air museum for that rich, packed past.
clues.narrowing: rules out capitals without such a dense cluster of old monuments

source.quote: The city has 320 monuments, all within an area of 0.55 square kilometres (0.21 sq mi), making it one of the most concentrated historic areas in the world.

clues.text: At just 0.61 square kilometres in size, this is the smallest capital city in the EU.
clues.narrowing: rules in the European Union's smallest capital city

source.quote: at just 0.61 square kilometres (0.24 sq mi), it is the European Union's smallest capital city

clues.text: A town in Oklahoma, in the south of the United States. It lies a short drive south of the state capital.
clues.narrowing: rules out all places outside the south central United States

source.quote: the second-most populous city in the Oklahoma City Metro Area after the state capital, Oklahoma City, 20 miles (32 kilometers) north of Norman

clues.text: This place sits in Tornado Alley. Storms here spin up tornados that come often and hit hard.
clues.narrowing: rules out places outside the storm-prone middle of the United States

source.quote: Norman lies within Tornado Alley, a geographic region colloquially known for frequent and intense tornadic activity.

clues.text: Crowds rushed in to settle here in the Land Run of 1889. The town was made a city two years later, in 1891.
clues.narrowing: rules out towns not founded in the 1889 land rush in this state

source.quote: The city was settled during the Land Run of 1889, which opened the former Unassigned Lands of Indian Territory to American pioneer settlement. It was named in honor of Abner Norman, the area's initial land surveyor, and was formally incorporated on May 13, 1891.

clues.text: A state school here holds a vast art trove. It is the largest gift of French Impressionist art to an American school.
clues.narrowing: points to the one town whose state school holds that record art gift

source.quote: which contains the largest collection of French Impressionist art ever given to an American university

clues.text: This is home to the University of Oklahoma. Its sports teams are the Sooners, and huge crowds pack their football games.
clues.narrowing: confirms the home of the Sooners and its state university

source.quote: home to the University of Oklahoma, the largest university in the state, with nearly 32,000 students. The university is well known for its sporting events by teams under the banner of the nickname "Sooners", with over 85,000 people routinely attending football games.
